title: Review: Titrations and solution calculations; Practical techniques and uncertainties; Ionic bonding and lattices
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AQA A-level Chemistry (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: BD01#t2 term and clue written for the game; BD01#t4 term and clue written for the game; AM08b#t1 term and clue written for the game; PR01b#t1 term and clue written for the game. Questions: AM08b#N.10, BD01#N.3a, PR01a#N.13, PR01b#N.9, AM08b#N.5, BD01#N.15, PR01a#N.12, AM08b#N.3, BD01#N.6, PR01a#N.10, BD01#N.14a, PR01a#N.5. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Anion
items.clue: A negatively charged particle formed when a non-metal atom gains electrons.

items.label: Giant ionic lattice
items.clue: A regular 3-D array of alternating positive and negative particles, with no molecules.

items.label: Back titration
items.clue: A known excess of acid is added to a sample, then the leftover acid is measured with alkali.

items.label: Volumetric flask
items.clue: One-mark glassware that contains a single exact amount of liquid; used for making solutions.

questions.stem: An impure sample of magnesium oxide, an insoluble base, is analysed by back titration. MgO(s) + 2HCl(aq) → MgCl₂(aq) + H₂O(l). Assume the impurities do not react with acid. 0.400 g of the sample is added to 25.0 cm³ of 1.00 mol dm⁻³ HCl (excess). The leftover acid needs 14.30 cm³ of 0.500 mol dm⁻³ NaOH. What is the percentage by mass of MgO in the sample? (Aᵣ: O 16.0, Mg 24.3)
An atom of element X has the electron configuration 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p⁴. Which ion does X form in its ionic compounds?

options.text: X²⁺
X⁶⁺
X²⁻
X⁶⁻

questions.explanation: Six outer electrons (3s² 3p⁴). X gains two to reach 3s² 3p⁶: 16 protons, 18 electrons, charge 2−. X is sulfur: S²⁻.

questions.stem: A student mixes two solutions in a polystyrene cup to find an enthalpy change. The thermometer has an uncertainty of ±0.5 °C per reading, and the temperature rises by only about 4 °C. Which change would most reduce the percentage uncertainty in the temperature change, ΔT? -

options.text: Use larger volumes of the same two solutions.
Use more concentrated solutions, keeping the same volumes.
Start with both solutions at a higher temperature.
Record each temperature to two decimal places.

questions.explanation: More reacts in the same volume, so ΔT is larger (e.g. about 20 °C). The ±1.0 °C uncertainty in ΔT is then about 5% instead of 25%.

questions.stem: A student must heat a reaction mixture containing ethanol (highly flammable, boiling point 78 °C) for 30 minutes. Which plan best controls the risk?

options.text: Heat it over a Bunsen burner on a low flame, in a fume cupboard.
Heat it over a Bunsen burner, wearing gloves and eye protection.
Heat it under reflux, using a water bath or an electric heater.
Heat it in an open beaker so that the vapour can escape.

questions.explanation: No naked flame, and the condenser returns ethanol vapour to the flask, so little escapes.

questions.stem: 10.0 cm³ of vinegar is diluted to 100.0 cm³ in a volumetric flask. A 25.0 cm³ portion needs 20.75 cm³ of 0.100 mol dm⁻³ NaOH. CH₃COOH + NaOH → CH₃COONa + H₂O. What was the concentration of ethanoic acid in the original vinegar, in mol dm⁻³?
questions.explanation: n(NaOH) = 0.100 × 0.02075 = 2.075 × 10⁻³ mol = n(acid) in the portion. 2.075 × 10⁻³ ÷ 0.0250 = 0.0830 diluted; × 10 = 0.830 in the vinegar.

questions.stem: In a kettle's heating element, the hot metal wire is packed in powdered magnesium oxide, MgO, inside a metal tube. MgO is ionic, yet it is used here as an electrical insulator. Why doesn't it conduct?

options.text: MgO contains no ions until it is dissolved or melted.
Its ions are held in fixed positions, and MgO stays solid at the element's temperature.
Its electrons are all shared in covalent bonds, so none are free to move.
Its ions are too highly charged to move, even when MgO is molten.

questions.explanation: Charge flows only if charged particles can move. In the solid the ions are locked in the lattice and there are no free electrons. Strong 2+/2− attractions keep MgO solid to about 2850 °C.

questions.stem: A student plots the volume of gas collected against time. The line of best fit is straight, but does not pass through the origin. It passes through (10 s, 14 cm³) and (50 s, 62 cm³). What is the gradient, in cm³ s⁻¹?
questions.explanation: (62 − 14) ÷ (50 − 10) = 48 ÷ 40 = 1.2. The line meets the y-axis at 2 cm³, so one point alone gives the wrong answer.

questions.stem: In a back titration, an insoluble carbonate is added to excess hydrochloric acid, and the leftover acid is titrated with sodium hydroxide. Which amount equals the moles of HCl that reacted with the carbonate?

options.text: The moles of NaOH used in the titration of the leftover acid
The moles of HCl added to the solid at the very start
The moles of HCl added minus the moles of NaOH used in the titre
Half the moles of NaOH used in the titration of the leftover acid

questions.explanation: HCl reacts 1 : 1 with NaOH, so n(NaOH) = acid left over. Subtract it from the acid added to get the acid the carbonate used.

options.text: NH₄SO₄ for ammonium sulfate
NaCO₃ for sodium carbonate
Ca(OH)₂ for calcium hydroxide
AlNO₃ for aluminium nitrate

questions.explanation: One Ca²⁺ (2+) is balanced by two OH⁻ (2 × 1−). The bracket keeps each hydroxide ion whole.

questions.stem: A student dissolves 2.5 g of NaCl (M = 58.5 g mol⁻¹) in water and makes the solution up to 250.0 cm³. Which value of the concentration, in mol dm⁻³, is given to the appropriate number of significant figures?
questions.explanation: 2.5 ÷ 58.5 ÷ 0.2500 = 0.1709… The mass has only 2 significant figures, so the answer has 2: 0.17.

questions.stem: Ionic radii (pm): Na⁺ 102, K⁺ 138, F⁻ 133, Cl⁻ 181. Which shows the strength of the ionic bonding in NaF, NaCl and KCl in decreasing order?

options.text: KCl > NaCl > NaF
NaF > NaCl > KCl
NaF > KCl > NaCl
NaF = NaCl = KCl

questions.explanation: All are 1+ and 1−, so radii decide. Radius sums: NaF 235, NaCl 283, KCl 319 pm. Closer centres, stronger attraction.

questions.stem: A burette reading has an uncertainty of ±0.05 cm³. A student's titre is 12.50 cm³, found from two readings. What is the percentage uncertainty in the titre?
